messages:
alejandro: Heads-up — we're pausing the current release train effective now :warning:. We're seeing unexpected GPU node evictions in us-west that could impact canary throughput. Pause window ~36h, will reassess earlier if infra stabilizes. If you have in-flight canaries, we'll attempt graceful handoffs.

deploy-bot: [automated] canary-check triggered: 12/48 canaries degraded in us-west. See /ops/canary-dashboard

samira: How do we request an exception for an urgent enterprise patch? :thinking:

alejandro: @samira — open a release-exception ticket in the release-train board and ping me + @ops-oncall. Exceptions are limited to P0 customer hotfixes only. We'll triage within 30m.

linda: For teams on Dedicated pools, does this affect reserved capacity? We have an active commit for next week.

ops-oncall: Dedicated pools unaffected by the node evictions in us-west, but autoscaler may shift capacity. If you rely on strict SLAs, escalate to infra-allocations channel. :eyes:

matt: FYI this will push the hotfix window. We should move any non-critical deploys off the train to next window. :arrow_right:

alejandro: Canary reassignment plan: we'll reassign some canaries to eu-west and apac-regional slots to keep validation moving. If your canary needs specific infra, add a comment to the canary ticket with `infra:pin=us-west` and we'll not move it.

deploy-bot: command to check canary status:
```
rictl canary status --team=<team> --region=eu-west
```

Current owners of moved canaries will receive an automated DM.

alejandro: I'll post an update in 3h with status. Thanks for the quick coordination — try to avoid new train submissions until we confirm rebalancing. :thumbsup:
